import { Card, CardGrid, LinkCard } from "@astrojs/starlight/components";

Performance, inference and platform teams already run the loop that Thermite automates: change something, measure it, keep it if it is better. Agents can run that loop around the clock, but a team can only use what it can trust and govern. Thermite is built for that: agents only propose, code your team controls measures and decides, and every step is signed and recorded. It runs where your code and data already are.

## What to point it at

<CardGrid>
  <Card title="Inference cost" icon="rocket">
    A **hill climb** on tokens a second per GPU for the model you serve, on your production hardware,
    with guards that hold the outputs to today's.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Build and test time" icon="seti:config">
    A hill climb on a CI pipeline's minutes or a test suite's time, with every test still required
    to pass.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Migrations" icon="approve-check">
    A **goal campaign**: the codebase builds and passes its checks on the new framework or compiler,
    and on held-out tests the agents never saw. It ends when every goal is met.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Technical research" icon="magnifier">
    A **research** campaign for a design choice or due diligence: a report whose every claim rests on
    a quote that code checked against the archived page.
  </Card>
</CardGrid>

## Governance built in

- **Separation of duties, enforced.** Agents run as operating-system users that can neither read nor change the judge. The judge builds, runs and measures each change under users of its own, and only its verdict promotes a change. "The agent says it is faster" and "it is faster" stay separate ([Why agents never judge](../explanation/why-agents-never-judge.md), [Isolation inside a rig](../explanation/isolation.md)).
- **Signed commands, signed results.** Control signs every command it sends a rig, and the rig's harness signs every report. The supervisor in between carries both and can forge neither ([Trust between control and rigs](../explanation/trust.md)).
- **A complete record.** Each rig's ledger keeps every experiment, attempt, measurement and verdict, with the judge's reasons. Control keeps a copy of every rig's events, exports their results, and backs them up ([Back up and restore control](../how-to/operate/backup-and-restore.md)). Retention policies remove only what you choose, where and when you say ([Remove what Thermite keeps](../how-to/operate/retention-policies.md)).
- **People decide what matters.** Choose what waits for a person: new champions, audits, reviews and "not possible" endings. On a rig with an auditor, a model reads a surprisingly large win for anything that games the measurement before it is kept ([Decide what waits for you](../how-to/campaigns/decide-what-waits.md)).
- **Roles for people, scripts and agents.** One owner signs in to the dashboard and approves. Operator and agent tokens let scripts and AI assistants watch and steer, but never decide; a reader token lets a metrics scraper such as Prometheus read `/metrics` ([Tokens and roles](../reference/tokens.md)).
- **Keys go only where they are used.** Control seals every key, sign-in and kubeconfig you give it, and hands a rig only what that rig uses ([Who holds your keys](../explanation/who-holds-your-keys.md)).

## On your infrastructure

- **Kubernetes, your way.** Control sets a rig up in a namespace it creates, or in a slot your platform team made with a namespaced role and a resource quota. Network rules keep the harness to DNS, public addresses and the addresses you list, and the rig's isolation check fails if a lane can reach the cluster's API server ([Add a rig on a Kubernetes cluster](../how-to/install/rig-on-a-cluster.md)).
- **Machines and cloud GPUs.** Control also sets rigs up on machines over SSH, and launches them on RunPod with a spend limit.
- **Your images, repositories and models.** Build Thermite's images into your own registry, give rigs your private repositories with deploy keys, and point the agents at your own model endpoint or gateway ([Push the images to your own registry](../how-to/install/own-registry.md), [Use a private repository](../how-to/campaigns/private-repository.md), [Choose a model](../how-to/models/choose-a-model.md)).
- **One place to see every campaign.** One dashboard shows every campaign on every rig, with model use and cost per run. A REST API, MCP and the `thermite` command line give your tools the same actions ([Script Thermite with the REST API](../how-to/automate/rest-api.md)).

## What to know first

- **One owner for each installation.** Thermite is self-hosted and built for one researcher or one lab, not for separate customers sharing one installation. Each team runs its own control. There is no single sign-on.
- **API keys for shared use.** A Claude or ChatGPT plan may serve only its owner's own Thermite; a Thermite that several people use takes API keys.
- **Agents run code that a model wrote.** The harness reaches only DNS, the internet and its model endpoint, and on Kubernetes your network rules narrow that. On RunPod, Thermite adds no network rules. Read [the security model](../explanation/security-model.md) and [Known limits](../reference/known-limits.md).
- **Thermite is 0.x.** Versions make no upgrade promise yet. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0.

## Evaluate it

1. Read [the security model](../explanation/security-model.md): what each part can reach and what it trusts.
2. [Install on one machine](../tutorials/first-run.md) and watch the judge's smoke check give a dozen known cheats their expected verdicts.
3. [Run the stack](../how-to/install/one-machine.md) on a machine your team controls, with [images from your own registry](../how-to/install/own-registry.md).
4. [Add a rig on your cluster](../how-to/install/rig-on-a-cluster.md), in a slot your platform team made.
5. Give a pilot project its [kit](../how-to/campaigns/write-a-kit.md) and [contract](../how-to/campaigns/write-a-contract.md), and choose [what waits for you](../how-to/campaigns/decide-what-waits.md).
